extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, patentees, patent prosecutors, examiners, and parties appearing before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing practice before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (part 41 of 37 CFR), including ex parte appeals, inter partes reexaminations, depositions, expert testimony, and patent interferences. Covers filing times, brief content, amendment and evidence rules, motions, hearings, and interference procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General construction of Board rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.1(b): The Board’s rules must be construed to achieve just, speedy, and inexpensive resolutions of all Board proceedings (following the model of Rule 601 and Fed. R. Civ. P. 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the rules with an aim toward fairness, expedition, and cost-efficiency in all Board proceedings; this is an overarching interpretive principle for part 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of decorum in Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.1(c): The requirement for decorum under Rule 3 is explicitly extended to Board proceedings, including dealings with opposing parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties and counsel must maintain professional conduct and civility in correspondence and oral proceedings before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.2 preamble: Definitions in part 41 may change meaning depending on context; caution that a defined word may have a different meaning in particular circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting defined terms (e.g., 'Board', 'final', 'hearing', 'panel', 'party'), examine the context in which the term is used in the rules and statutes cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'Board' and 'Board member'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.2: 'Board' covers (1) panels of Board members for final agency action (scope like 35 U.S.C. 6(b)), (2) action by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge where delegated, and (3) non-final actions performed by other officials; 'Board member' follows 35 U.S.C. 6(a) (ex officio members listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines who may act and which actions are 'Board' actions; useful when identifying proper forum and appealability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.3: Delegation of petition authority to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge; decisions committed by statute to the Board are not subject to petitions for supervisory review; other petitions in contested cases may be decided by other officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions have set timelines and require payment of a standard petition fee; failure to timely file a petition is sufficient basis for dismissal or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and acceptance of untimely papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.4: Follows Rules 136(b) and 645 for extensions of time and acceptance of untimely papers; points parties to related timeliness rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established extension procedures; be mindful of separate timeliness rules related to Board proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of counsel conduct and disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.5: The Board is delegated authority under 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(2) and 32 to regulate counsel conduct in Board proceedings and to conduct counsel disqualification proceedings while the Board has jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for professional conduct and potential disqualification are enforced by the Board during its jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.6(a): Publicly available materials remain publicly available; sets basis for determining when special circumstances justify publication of a Board action under 35 U.S.C. 122(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may publish actions where special circumstances justify it; many interference records may eventually be made public consistent with practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate papers and expunging
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.7: Recodifies practice regarding duplicate papers and expunging of papers and generalizes it to all Board proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filing duplicative submissions; the Board retains authority to expunge unnecessary or duplicative filings from the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of real parties-in-interest and related proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.8(a)–(b): Parties must disclose real parties-in-interest and provide notice of related proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs and submissions must identify the real party in interest and list prior/pending related appeals, interferences, or judicial proceedings known to the party or its representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions by assignee excluding inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.9: Follows Rule 643 for action by an assignee to the exclusion of an inventor, generalized to all Board proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how assignees may act in Board proceedings when excluding inventors; consult rule for procedural specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence addresses and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.10–41.11: Adds correspondence addresses for Board proceedings and codifies prohibition of ex parte communications about contested cases with officials actually conducting the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communications must observe ex parte prohibition; use prescribed addresses and channels for correspondence with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.12: Codifies existing interference practice regarding citation of authority, generalized to all Board proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant authority in briefs and motions; follow Board expectations for citation format and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees associated with Board practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.20: Consolidates rules on fees associated with Board practice; sets petition fee and appeals-related fees; existing fee rules (Rules 22, 23, 25–28) continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to the petition and appeals fee schedules; Board fees relocated to §41.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and definitions for ex parte appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.30 et seq.: Subpart B sets rules for ex parte appeals under 35 U.S.C. 134 of rejections in national applications, reissue applications, or ex parte reexamination; defines 'proceeding', 'applicant', and 'owner' for this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the subpart B definitions and timing rules specifically to ex parte appeals and ex parte reexamination appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing appeal and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.31: Incorporates former Rule 191(a)-(d) with clearer subsectioning; sets the timing requirements for filing an appeal and related actions; cross-references extension rules moved to other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully track the statutory/ regulatory timelines for filing an appeal and related filings; missing deadlines has significant procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits after appeal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.33 (replacing former Rules 116 and 195): (a) Amendments filed after filing an appeal and prior to the brief may be admitted as provided in §1.116; (b) Amendments filed on/after filing a brief may be admitted only to cancel claims (if cancellation doesn't affect scope of other pending claims) or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form; (c) All other amendments after filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by specified sections; (d) Affidavits or other evidence filed after filing appeal and prior to brief may be admitted if the examiner determines they overcome all rejections under appeal and there is a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after appeal are tightly limited; treat post-appeal amendments and affidavits as exceptional and follow §1.116 standards for admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment and return of jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.35: The Board may relinquish jurisdiction and return an application to the examining operation to permit completion of processing before the Board decides the appeal; Board may take other appropriate action to complete the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues needing examiner attention are identified before docketing, the Board may return the case to the examiner; parties should expect such remands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief content and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.37: Appellant’s brief (now 'Appeal brief') must comply with many requirements: one copy required (not three); file within two months from notice of appeal; identify by name the real party in interest; identify all other prior or pending related proceedings; state status of all claims and identify those appealed; provide a concise explanation of the invention for each independent claim and identify means-plus-function/step-plus-function limitations with specification page and line references and drawing reference characters; provide a concise statement listing each ground of rejection presented for review; remove former rigid grouping-of-claims rule and require separate headings for each ground of rejection, with optional subheadings for claims or claim groups; include an evidence appendix stating where evidence was entered in the record; include a related proceedings appendix with copies of decisions; exclude any new or non-admitted amendments/affidavits/evidence from the brief; non-compliant briefs will receive notice of reasons for non-compliance and time to amend; periods are extendable under Rule 136 for patent apps and Rule 550(c) for reexams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed structural and content requirements carefully: properly identify parties and related proceedings, tie claim explanations to the specification (page/line), identify and substantiate every ground of rejection, include appendices for evidence and related decisions, and avoid including new evidence or amendments in briefs. Failure to argue separately for grouped claims results in waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new/amended evidence in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.37(c)(2) and related: Appellant's appeal brief must exclude any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attempt to include new evidence in the brief will result in exclusion or treatment as a request to reopen prosecution; rely on evidence of record only unless the Board/examiner admits new evidence under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds of rejection in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.39(a)(2): Examiner may include a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer (eliminating the former prohibition). New grounds should be rare, must be personally approved by a Technology Center Director or designee, and be prominently identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new arguments are raised in appellant’s brief, the examiner may respond with a new ground in the answer rather than reopening prosecution; MPEP guidance will set circumstances appropriate for such new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant response to new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.39(b): If examiner’s answer contains a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either (1) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under Rule 111 with or without amendment or evidence (which reopens prosecution), or (2) file a reply brief under §41.41 (to maintain the appeal), which may not include amendments or evidence. Failure to exercise one of these options within two months causes sua sponte dismissal as to claims subject to the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide promptly (two months) whether to reopen prosecution (submit amendments/evidence) or press the appeal (reply brief). A reply brief accompanied by amendment/evidence will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution and withdraw the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief limitations and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.41: A reply brief cannot include any new or non-admitted amendments, affidavits, or other evidence. A reply brief not in compliance will not be considered and the examiner will notify appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reply brief addresses only arguments and evidence already of record; do not submit new evidence in a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner’s answer to reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.43: Examiner may furnish a supplemental examiner’s answer to respond to any new issue raised in the reply brief (must be approved by Technology Center Director/designee). A supplemental examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection. If furnished, appellant may file another reply brief within two months from its date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental answers are limited to responding to new issues raised in reply briefs and cannot themselves raise new grounds; parties get another two-month period to reply to a supplemental answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request and hearing conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.47: Request for oral hearing must be a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' and filed within two months from the examiner’s answer or supplemental answer. At oral hearing, appellant may rely only on evidence previously considered by examiner and present arguments relied upon in brief or reply brief except as permitted on showing of good cause; primary examiner may rely only on arguments/evidence in answer or supplemental answer; appellant opens and concludes the argument; in limited circumstances (good cause) new arguments based on recent Board or Federal Court decisions may be raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File oral hearing requests timely and use hearing time to present arguments based on the record; new arguments are permitted only on a showing of good cause and typically must be based on new legal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision roles: affirm/reverse/remand and conforming amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.50(a)(1),(c): The Board may affirm or reverse the examiner's decision in whole or in part on grounds/claims specified by the examiner, or remand to examiner. The Board’s opinion may explicitly state how a claim on appeal could be amended to overcome a specific rejection; appellant then has the right to amend in conformity with such statement, but the examiner may still reject the amended claim if the rejection constitutes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board opinions can provide guidance for conforming amendments to overcome specific rejections; such amendments are permitted but subject to new-ground scrutiny by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to respond to Board order or remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.50(a)(2) and related: Appellant must respond to supplemental examiner’s answer issued after remand (either request reopening/prosecution or request to maintain appeal by reply brief) to avoid sua sponte dismissal of the appeal for the claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely action after remand is essential to avoid dismissal; options mirror those for a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition notice and content requirements in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections in Subpart D (sample): Notice of deposition must state place, time, identity of witness, list of items to be produced, and general description of scope and nature of testimony to be elicited; objections to defects in notice are waived unless a motion to quash is promptly filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve a complete deposition notice; promptly move to quash defects to preserve objections; include interpreter arrangements early for foreign-language depositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of taking depositions and transcript formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D provisions: Witness sworn by authorized officer; testimony taken in Q&A order recorded by officer or disinterested person (unless waived); exhibits must be numbered and served; objections at deposition must be noted on record; witness should read and sign the transcript unless waived or refused; officer must prepare certified transcript with specified certificate content; officer must promptly provide transcript copies to parties and proponent files original exhibit; objections to content/form/qualifications are waived unless made on record and preserved in timely filed miscellaneous motion to exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formal deposition procedures strictly to preserve objections and admissibility; ensure certified transcript contains required certificate statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of testimony and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D: Except as Board orders or parties agree, the proponent of testimony bears all costs, including reasonable costs to make witness available for cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for and allocate deposition costs; seek Board orders if cost allocation should differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony and tests/data standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.158: (a) Expert testimony that does not disclose the underlying facts or data on which the opinion is based is entitled to little or no weight; testimony on U.S. patent law will not be admitted. (b) If a party relies on a technical test or data, it must provide an affidavit explaining (1) why the test/data is used, (2) how the test was performed and data generated, (3) how the data is used to determine a value, (4) how the test is regarded in the relevant art, and (5) any other information necessary for the Board to evaluate the test and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full factual and methodological disclosure for expert opinions and tests; unsupported expert conclusions are given little weight and legal-opinion testimony on patent law is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable construction and pendency goal for interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.200(b)-(c): A claim shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the application or patent in which it appears; patent interferences shall be administered such that pendency before the Board is normally no more than two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broadest reasonable claim construction for interference proceedings; Board aims to resolve interferences within ~2 years of pendency when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions specific to interferences (counts, involved claim, threshold issue, senior/junior party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.201: 'Count' defines the interfering subject matter and scope of admissible proofs; 'involved claim' is a claim designated as corresponding to the count; 'senior party' is entitled to presumption of prior invention based on accorded benefit; 'threshold issue' examples include no interference-in-fact, repose, or lack of written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand interference-specific terms as they control admissibility of proofs, presumptions, and early threshold motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to suggest an interference (applicant obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.202(a): An applicant suggesting an interference must: (1) identify the application/patent, (2) identify all claims believed to interfere, propose one or more counts, and show claim correspondence to counts, (3) provide for each count a claim chart comparing at least one claim of each party and show why claims interfere per §41.203(a), (4) explain in detail why applicant will prevail on priority, (5) if a claim was added/amended to provoke interference, provide claim chart showing written description for each claim in applicant's spec, and (6) for each constructive reduction to practice for which benefit is sought, provide a chart showing where disclosure provides a constructive reduction to practice within the interfering subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions to declare an interference require detailed claim charts, correspondence to counts, priority arguments, and written-description/benefit proof; incomplete suggestions may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's authority to require added claims to provoke interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.202(c): An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy requirement in the set period operates as concession of priority for that subject matter. The proposed claim must be patentable to the applicant and drawn to patentable subject matter claimed by another party (apart from 102(g) priority question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply promptly with examiner's requirement to add claims to provoke interference or risk concession of priority; ensure added claim meets patentability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration content for interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.203(b): Notice declaring an interference must identify the interfering subject matter, the involved applications/patents/claims, the accorded benefit for each count, and the claims corresponding to each count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration sets the scope of the proceeding and the initial presumptions of benefit and correspondence; parties should review declaration carefully for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority statement and limitations on evidence of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.204(a): A party may not submit evidence of its priority in addition to accorded benefit unless it files a priority statement setting forth all bases to establish entitlement to judgment on priority. The priority statement must state date/location of earliest corroborated conception, date/location of earliest corroborated actual reduction to practice, earliest corroborated diligence date, and provide a copy of earliest document relied upon for conception. If a junior party fails to file a priority statement overcoming a senior party’s accorded benefit, judgment is entered against the junior party absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority evidence beyond accorded benefit requires a detailed priority statement with corroborated dates and documentary proof; failure to file can be dispositive for junior parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and sufficiency of motions in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.208: Substantive motions in an interference must (a) raise a threshold issue, (b) seek to change the scope of interfering subject matter or claim correspondence, (c) seek to change benefit accorded, or (d) seek judgment on derivation or priority. A motion must provide a showing, supported with appropriate evidence, such that, if unrebutted, it would justify the relief sought; the burden of proof is on the movant. To be sufficient when adding/amending a claim or count, the movant must show patentability (claim or count) over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft motions in interference with a clear legal basis, evidentiary support, and proof of patentability when adding/amending claims or counts; anticipate and meet the movant’s burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements filing and access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.205: Agreements made in connection with termination of an interference must be filed prior to termination; Chief APJ may permit filing up to six months after termination with petition and showing of good cause; parties may request agreements be kept separate from interference file and restrict access (subject to petition and good cause), with government agencies given access on written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File settlement agreements timely; use separate-file requests to control public access if necessary, subject to Board rules on access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions regarding priority and claim correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.207: (a) Parties are presumed to have invented in order of dates of their accorded benefit for each count; (a)(2) Priority proof by preponderance except clear and convincing evidence required if earliest constructive reduction to practice is after issue/publication date of an involved patent/application; (b) All claims of a party corresponding to the count are presumed to stand or fall together and challenge requires timely substantive motion; (c) When a motion for judgment of unpatentability against an opponent’s claim on prior art is granted, movant’s claims corresponding to same count will be presumed unpatentable unless movant rebuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know and plan for presumptions: accorded benefit drives presumptive order of invention; higher evidentiary standard applies if priority date is after certain public dates; challenge claim correspondence timely; anticipate cross-applicability of prior-art judgments.
